pr_title: Change year max digits for strict_date_optional_time and date_optional_time
pr_body:
We changed the default joda behaviour in `strict_date_optional_time` to
max 4 digits in a year. Java.time implementation should behave the same way.
At the same time `date_optional_time` should have 9digits for year part.

closes #52396
closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/72191

issue_context.title: ES 7 changes which dates `date_optional_time` can successfully parse
comments: @pgomulka do you have an opinion on this? I see we accepted up to 9 digits in 6.8 (I see from an error message in 6.8 that "year must be in the range [-292275055,292278994]") but maybe the restriction to 5 digits was introduced in 7x on purpose and this should be a documentation issue? I don't know all the background around these decisions I'm afraid.

this might be a bug. As stated in joda 'non strict' `date_optional_time` had year of length 4-9
the `strict_date_optional_time` which is a modified ES version had it changed to year of lenght 4-4
I was about to fix this https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/54260 but I forgot about this PR.
I will try to update the linked PR with the fix for the `date_optional_time` as well

review_comments: Isn't this a breaking change? And it then limits the ability to use dates in the future (yes past 9999)? Is the expectation then that dates in the distant future must use epoch seconds or millis?

we have accidentally changed  the max length of year in strict_date_optional_time in 7.0.
If we do not consider this accidental change a bug, then agree it would be a breaking change. 
This change - limiting the length from 10 to 4 - might help parsing epoch millis with length between 4 and 10. At the moment the "date":1234567890 would be considered a year.
I think most of the time users are actually using the dates around our time, not so much in the future. So your suggestion that they should use epoch seconds/millis (or custom format) for such a dates makes sense to me.
